summary: Rewrote godot/scripts/core/save_section_pending_commands.gd to SAVE-P2-R02 v1 as a single unified patch artifact at docs/validation/evidence/save-pending-2026-09-19/codec.patch. Capture now zero-fills a full arena once and copies each live payload to its own saved offset (bounds-checked per span before any write), so allocation/key-order disagreement, partial-drain holes and dead tails survive verbatim; arena_rebuild_refusal no longer demands contiguity/zero base/length-sum and instead re-runs shape and bound gates (safe on malformed Records) then span-shape, overlap and zero-dead-byte validation. apply() gained a binding gate requiring a non-null record and both stores, the SAME actual SimClock object shared by both queues, that clock's completed tick equal to saved_completed_tick and its load barrier held, keeping the existing both-queues-empty requirement; it then validates the whole Record, the SCHQ0001 extension and the packed economic window (built once, at most 262144 bytes, plus the used arena prefix) through commands.gd::pending_window_refusal() before any mutation. Install order is commands first via restore_pending_window, scheduler second via its atomic restore_extension; a scheduler refusal restores the prior EMPTY window and the exact prior allocator pair through the same new owner API, checks that bool, reports the scheduler refusal on successful recovery and the distinct SAVE_PC_ROLLBACK_FAILED (new constant) with an explicit uncertainty message and held barrier otherwise. No fallible step follows scheduler success. restore_sequence/admit_stamped_into paths, the per-row Command admission loop and the old envelope preflight are gone; owner diagnostics are formatted through a helper that states a fallback when an owner returns false with an empty code. Schema 2, the 24-byte prefix, 64/32-byte records, ordinals and the exhausted-allocator refusal behaviour are untouched. Module docs replaced the misleading BLOCKER P2 / restore_sequence / admit_stamped text with the current contract plus a bounded cold-scratch note.

+			prior_high, prior_low):
+		return SaveHeader.Refusal.new(REFUSE_ROLLBACK_FAILED,
+			("scheduler_events.gd refused a subsection its own validator accepted (%s), and "
+				+ "commands.gd then refused to reinstall the empty window and allocator "
+				+ "(%d, %d) it held before (%s). This module cannot say what the command queue "
+				+ "now holds; it claims no rollback, releases no barrier and leaves the load "
+				+ "open for the coordinator.")
+				% [failure, prior_high, prior_low, _owner_detail(commands_store.last_refusal())])
+	return SaveHeader.Refusal.new(REFUSE_STORE_REFUSED,
+		("scheduler_events.gd refused a subsection its own validator accepted: %s. The command "
+			+ "queue was reinstalled as the empty window and allocator (%d, %d) it held before.")
+			% [failure, prior_high, prior_low])
+
+
+static func _owner_detail(code: StringName) -> String:
+	"""An owner's refusal code, or a stated fallback when it answered false and published none.
+
+	Both owners report some failures through a bool alone, so formatting the bare code would
+	produce a message that reads as if no failure had been described. Saying so explicitly is
+	the difference between an unexplained refusal and one that names its own silence.
+	"""
+	if code == REFUSE_NONE:
+		return "it published no refusal code"
+	return String(code)
